content: Clarithromycin is contraindicated in patients who have a known hypersensitivity to clarithromycin, any of its excipients, erythromycin, or any other macrolide antibiotics. Clarithromycin should not be used in patients with a history of cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction that was associated with prior use of clarithromycin. The concurrent administration of clarithromycin with cisapride, pimozide, astemizole, terfenadine, ergotamine, or dihydroergotamine is contraindicated. Post-marketing reports have documented drug interactions when clarithromycin or erythromycin is co-administered with cisapride, pimozide, astemizole, or terfenadine, leading to cardiac arrhythmias such as QT prolongation, ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, and torsades de pointes. These effects are likely due to the inhibition of the metabolism of these drugs by clarithromycin and erythromycin. Fatalities have been reported in such cases. The concomitant use of clarithromycin and colchicine is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Clarithromycin should not be administered to patients with a history of QT prolongation or ventricular cardiac arrhythmias, including torsades de pointes. Clarithromycin must not be used concurrently with HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (statins) that are extensively metabolized by CYP3A4, such as lovastatin or simvastatin, due to the increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. For information regarding contraindications of other drugs indicated for use in combination with Biaxin, refer to the CONTRAINDICATIONS section of their respective package inserts.
